title: Colorectal cancer: adenoma–carcinoma sequence, TNM staging and the histology report

header.contentArea: Pathology (histology report with a clinical scenario)

related.why: Anatomy of the rectum and anal canal

brief.scenario: Mr Thomas Wright, 62, was referred on the suspected cancer pathway with rectal bleeding and change in bowel habit. Colonoscopy showed a sigmoid adenocarcinoma. He has had a sigmoid colectomy. The examiner will give you his staging and histology results in stages.
brief.task: Explain how this cancer developed, interpret the staging and histology results, and say what happens next.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Sequence, then read the report: T, N, M, stage, then MMR, then what next.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling a tumour through the visceral peritoneum T3, or ignoring node yield.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll read the T, N and M stage, the node count and the margins."

grid.label: Adenoma–carcinoma sequence
grid.fail: Cannot describe how a polyp becomes a cancer.
grid.pass: Stepwise: normal mucosa, adenoma, dysplasia, carcinoma; APC loss early, then KRAS, then TP53 late (chromosomal instability).
grid.high: Names the mismatch repair-deficient pathway and the serrated pathway (BRAF, CpG methylation); explains why removing adenomas prevents cancer.

grid.label: T stage
grid.fail: Calls a tumour through the visceral peritoneum T3.
grid.pass: T3 into pericolorectal tissue; T4a penetrates the visceral peritoneum; T4b invades or adheres to other organs. This is pT4a.
grid.high: Links pT4 to peritoneal recurrence, and knows NICE NG151 suggests considering preoperative chemotherapy for cT4 colon cancer.

grid.label: N stage and node yield
grid.fail: Miscounts the node stage or ignores how many nodes were examined.
grid.pass: 2 of 16 nodes positive: N1b. N1 is 1–3 nodes, N2 is 4 or more. Checks at least 12 nodes were examined.
grid.high: Gives N1a one node, N1c tumour deposits without nodes, N2a 4–6, N2b 7 or more.

grid.label: M stage and overall stage
grid.fail: Stages the tumour without chest imaging or M stage.
grid.pass: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no metastases: pT4a N1b M0, stage III (IIIB).
grid.high: M1a one organ, M1b more than one organ, M1c peritoneal metastases.

grid.label: Adjuvant treatment
grid.fail: Says no further treatment is needed because the tumour is out.
grid.pass: Stage III: MDT and oncology referral. NICE NG151 offers CAPOX for 3 months; FOLFOX or capecitabine alone if unsuitable.
grid.high: Notes NG151 bases the choice on pT4 and/or pN2, fitness, comorbidity and preference.

grid.label: Revised report: stage II
grid.fail: Calls pT4a N0 with 9 nodes examined low risk.
grid.pass: pT4a N0 is stage II; pT4 and fewer than 12 nodes are high-risk features, so adjuvant chemotherapy is discussed at MDT.
grid.high: Knows NG151 makes no stage II recommendation; ESMO: high-risk stage II may add oxaliplatin; MMR deficiency lowers fluoropyrimidine benefit.

grid.label: Mismatch repair testing
grid.fail: Does not test for mismatch repair, or delays treatment waiting for it.
grid.pass: All colorectal cancers tested at diagnosis (NICE DG27). MLH1 and PMS2 lost: BRAF V600E test, then MLH1 promoter hypermethylation if BRAF negative.
grid.high: Refers for germline Lynch testing if both are negative; MSH2, MSH6 or PMS2 loss goes straight to germline testing.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It just grows from the bowel lining.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The report says the tumour penetrates the visceral peritoneum. T stage?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Stage II. I don't think we need more scans.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's been removed, so follow-up only.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: If it had been N0 with only 9 nodes?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Immunohistochemistry shows loss of MLH1 and PMS2.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure; I'd wait for that before planning treatment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mostly stepwise: normal mucosa, adenoma, dysplasia, carcinoma. APC is lost early, then KRAS, then TP53 late.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Through the visceral peritoneum is T4a. T3 would be into pericolorectal fat; T4b into another organ.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: 2 of 16 positive: N1b. N1 is 1 to 3 nodes, N2 is 4 or more. 16 nodes is an adequate yield.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis is clear. Overall stage?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: pT4a N1b M0: stage III, IIIB.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: MDT discussion and oncology referral. NICE recommends CAPOX for 3 months, or FOLFOX or capecitabine alone if that's unsuitable.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: If it had been N0 with 9 nodes?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Stage II, but pT4 and fewer than 12 nodes are both high-risk, so adjuvant chemotherapy would be discussed at MDT.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That's mismatch repair deficiency. Next is BRAF V600E, then MLH1 promoter hypermethylation if BRAF is negative.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes. Mismatch repair-deficient tumours are microsatellite unstable, as in Lynch syndrome. The serrated pathway involves BRAF and CpG methylation. Because most cancers pass through an adenoma, removing adenomas prevents cancer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Peritoneal penetration raises the risk of peritoneal recurrence. If CT had shown cT4 before surgery, NICE NG151 says consider preoperative chemotherapy.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: N1a one node, N1b two or three, N1c tumour deposits without nodal disease. N2a 4 to 6, N2b 7 or more.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: M1a one organ, M1b more than one, M1c peritoneal.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you choose his regimen?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE NG151 bases it on pT4 and/or pN2, performance status, comorbidity and his preference. He's pT4, so oncology will weigh that.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NG151 has no stage II recommendation. ESMO suggests high-risk stage II may add oxaliplatin, and mismatch repair deficiency reduces fluoropyrimidine benefit.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: BRAF and methylation are both negative.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Then this may be Lynch syndrome: refer for germline testing, with counselling. Loss of MSH2 or MSH6 would have gone straight to germline testing.

failures.consequence: Understages the tumour and misses a high-risk feature.

failures.move: Offering follow-up only for node-positive disease.
failures.consequence: Denies him adjuvant chemotherapy that NICE recommends for stage III.
Treats a possibly understaged tumour as low risk.
Misses Lynch syndrome in him and his relatives.

recovery.line: I'll go through T, N with node yield, M, margins, then mismatch repair.
That depends on high-risk features and mismatch repair status, and is an MDT decision.

knowledge.fact: T4a: through visceral peritoneum. T4b: into other organs.
N1: 1–3 nodes (N1c deposits only). N2: 4 or more. M1a one organ, M1b more than one, M1c peritoneum.
Stage III colon: CAPOX 3 months; FOLFOX or capecitabine alone if unsuitable.
Stage II high-risk: pT4, fewer than 12 nodes.
Test all colorectal cancers for mismatch repair at diagnosis; MLH1 loss: BRAF, then methylation, then germline.

recall.say: "pT4a N1b M0: stage III, for MDT and adjuvant chemotherapy."

numbers.meaning: CAPOX for stage III colon cancer

recall.trap: Peritoneal penetration is T4a, not T3.
recall.finish: Adjuvant chemotherapy; germline testing if Lynch suspected.

sources.name: Brierley JD, Gospodarowicz MK, Wittekind C (eds). UICC TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours
sources.supports: Colorectal T, N and M categories and stage groups (T4a, T4b, N1a–c, N2a–b, M1a–c; T4a N1 M0 = IIIB)

sources.name: NICE guideline NG151: Colorectal cancer
sources.supports: Stage III colon cancer adjuvant options (CAPOX 3 months; FOLFOX 3–6 months or single-agent fluoropyrimidine 6 months if unsuitable) chosen by pT4 and/or pN2, fitness and preference; consider preoperative systemic therapy for cT4 colon cancer

sources.name: NICE diagnostics guidance DG27 (now HealthTech guidance HTG430): Molecular testing strategies for Lynch syndrome in people with colorectal cancer
sources.supports: Test all colorectal cancers at diagnosis by MMR immunohistochemistry or MSI; MLH1 loss: BRAF V600E then MLH1 promoter hypermethylation; germline testing if negative or if MSH2, MSH6 or PMS2 abnormal; do not delay treatment

sources.name: Argilés G, et al. Localised colon cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Ann Oncol 2020;31:1291-1305
sources.supports: At least 12 lymph nodes; pT4 and fewer than 12 nodes as major stage II risk factors; high-risk stage II may add oxaliplatin; MSI/dMMR gives better prognosis and less benefit from adjuvant therapy

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Colorectal cancer presentation, staging investigations and multidisciplinary management

partner.opening: Mr Wright has had a sigmoid colectomy for adenocarcinoma. First, how does colorectal cancer develop?

reveals.finding: Histology: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 42 mm, extending through the muscularis propria and penetrating the visceral peritoneal surface. Margins clear.
Two of 16 regional nodes contain metastatic carcinoma. No tumour deposits.
Preoperative CT chest, abdomen and pelvis: no distant metastases.
Revised: 0 of 9 nodes involved; everything else unchanged.
MMR immunohistochemistry: loss of MLH1 and PMS2; MSH2 and MSH6 retained.

push.question: What happens next?
push.expect: MDT; adjuvant CAPOX per NICE NG151.

push.question: What does loss of MLH1 and PMS2 mean?
push.expect: dMMR; BRAF then methylation; germline if negative.

curveballs.prompt: The tumour was stuck to the bladder and removed en bloc, with tumour in the bladder wall.
curveballs.safeAnswer: That is T4b: direct invasion of another organ.

curveballs.prompt: There are tumour deposits in the mesentery but no positive nodes.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Points to a sporadic tumour from MLH1 methylation; Lynch syndrome is unlikely and further germline testing is not routinely needed.

curveballs.prompt: Should we wait for the MMR result before starting chemotherapy?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. NICE DG27 says do not wait for results before starting treatment.
